extra.message: The 'id' query parameter (params['id'][0]) is concatenated directly into a SQL SELECT statement passed to cursor.execute(). An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. id=1 UNION SELECT ...) to read passwords/sessions from the users table.

In AuthBypass.run(), the 'password' parameter (and 'username' after partial sanitization) are concatenated directly into a SQL query passed to cursor.execute(). A payload like password=' OR '1'='1 allows authentication bypass / SQL injection.

In CommandInjection.run(), the user-controlled 'domain' parameter is joined into a shell command string and passed to subprocess.check_output() with shell=True. An attacker can inject OS commands (e.g. domain=google.com;id) to execute arbitrary commands on the server.

In do_BDR(), the raw request path (self.path[1:]) is passed directly to subprocess.check_output() with shell=True. Any client can supply an arbitrary shell command in the URL path, yielding full remote command execution (gated only by risk level).

In UnsafeDeserialization.run(), the user-supplied 'object' parameter is base64-decoded and passed to pickle.loads(). Deserializing attacker-controlled pickle data allows arbitrary code execution via crafted __reduce__ payloads.

In PathTraversal.run(), the user-controlled 'path' parameter is passed to os.path.abspath() and open() without any validation against a base directory. An attacker can read arbitrary files (e.g. path=/etc/passwd or path=../../etc/passwd).

In PathTraversal.run(), when the 'path' parameter contains '://' it is passed directly to urllib.request.urlopen(). An attacker can force the server to fetch arbitrary URLs (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/ metadata, internal services, or file:// URIs), enabling Server-Side Request Forgery.

In StaticHandler.find(), the user-controlled request path is interpolated into open('./{}'.format(path)) without normalization or restriction to a static directory. Crafted paths containing '../' allow reading arbitrary files outside the intended static directory.
In StaticHandler.find(), the user-controlled request path is interpolated into open('./{}'.format(path)) without normalization. Crafted paths with '../' sequences allow arbitrary file read.
In XSSReflected.run(), the user-supplied 'msg' parameter is returned and embedded into the HTML response without any output encoding, allowing reflected Cross-Site Scripting.

In XSSStored.run(), the 'comment' parameter is stored in the database and later rendered directly into HTML (line 97) without escaping, allowing stored Cross-Site Scripting that executes for every visitor of the guestbook.

In UnvalidatedRedirect.run(), the user-controlled 'path' parameter is interpolated into a JavaScript window.location.replace() call without validation, enabling open redirect to arbitrary sites and DOM-based XSS (e.g. path=');alert(1);// ).
In SessionFixation.run(), the user-controlled 'path' parameter is interpolated into a JavaScript window.location assignment without validation, enabling open redirect and DOM-based XSS.

In SessionFixation.run(), the user-supplied 'session' parameter is set directly as the victim's SESSIONID cookie. An attacker can fix a known session identifier on the victim, then hijack the authenticated session after login.

In ExecutionAfterRedirect.run(), the sensitive admin content (Manage Users / Update Database Settings) is included in the response body before the client-side redirect to /login. Because authorization is enforced only via a JavaScript redirect rather than server-side, unauthenticated users can read the protected content.

In XSRequestForgery.run(), the user's email is updated via a state-changing GET request with no anti-CSRF token. An attacker can forge a request (e.g. an image/link) to change a logged-in victim's email address.

In Clickjacking.run(), the user account is deleted via a state-changing GET request with no anti-CSRF token and no clickjacking protection (no X-Frame-Options). An attacker can trick a logged-in victim into deleting their account.
In AuthBypass.run(), hardcoded credentials username 'dsvpwa' / password 'dsvpwa' are accepted for authentication, providing a backdoor login.

Session tokens are generated using random.sample() over the standard library 'random' module, which is a non-cryptographic PRNG. Predictable session tokens can be guessed/brute-forced, enabling session hijacking. Use the 'secrets' module instead.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak PRNG

extra.message: The response explicitly sets 'X-XSS-Protection: 0', disabling the browser's built-in XSS auditor and weakening defense against reflected XSS.
The Content-Security-Policy is set to "default-src * 'unsafe-inline'", which allows scripts from any origin and inline script execution, effectively negating CSP protection against XSS.
Session cookies are emitted without the HttpOnly or Secure attributes (only 'path' is set). This exposes the SESSIONID cookie to theft via JavaScript (XSS) and transmission over unencrypted HTTP.

The SSL context re-enables SSLv3 (clears OP_NO_SSLv3), enables TLS compression (clears OP_NO_COMPRESSION, vulnerable to CRIME), and disables server cipher preference. This results in a weak/insecure TLS configuration.
SQL OperationalError exception objects are returned directly to the client, leaking internal database error details that aid SQL injection exploitation.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: In SQLinjection.run(), database column values (including attacker-injected UNION SELECT data) are rendered directly into HTML <td> elements without escaping, allowing cross-site scripting.
